cards.front: What should you know about two main types?
cards.back: Formal letters (to officials, businesses, newspapers) and Informal letters (to friends and family). The exam usually requires formal letters.

cards.front: What should you know about salutations?
cards.back: Dear Mr/Mrs/Ms [Surname] - if you know the name Dear Sir/Madam - if you don't know the name To the Editor - for letters to newspapers

cards.front: What should you know about sign-offs?
cards.back: "Yours sincerely" - if you used a name (Dear Mr Smith) "Yours faithfully" - if you used Dear Sir/Madam

cards.front: What should you know about top tip?
cards.back: In exams, you're almost always asked to write a formal letter. Avoid contractions and slang. Use sophisticated vocabulary appropriately.

cards.front: What should you know about purpose?
cards.back: To express an opinion, agree/disagree with an article, or raise awareness about an issue.

cards.front: What should you know about examiner's tip?
cards.back: Get the format right straight away. Write your address, skip a line, write the date, then the recipient's address. This sets up your letter correctly and shows you understand the conventions.

cards.front: What should you know about letter writing exam strategy?
cards.back: You have 45 minutes (40 marks: 24 AO5 + 16 AO6). Format marks are easy to earn — get them right first. First 2 minutes: Write your address (invent one), skip a line, write the date, then the recipient's address. This sets up the correct format immediately. Next 3 minutes: Plan your key arguments and the sign-off you'll use. Check: do you know the recipient's name? This determines "sincerely" vs "faithfully".
